# Turn a request into a testable product specification

Use this skill when you need the “what” and “why” of a change before anyone designs or implements it. It turns a prompt into a specification with functional, UX and UI layers, explicit non-goals and acceptance criteria.

## When to use it

Use `specify` for new features, product changes, user-facing behavior, or any request whose meaning could be interpreted several ways. Use [investigate](#skill-investigate) instead when something is already broken.

## What you need

Bring the problem, the intended user or operator, constraints and any known non-goals. You do not need the implementation design yet.

## Try it

Slash-command harnesses:

```text
/specify Add CSV export to HarborTasks. Export all tasks matching the current
project and filter, not only the visible page. Include only fields the user may view.
Empty results should still download a CSV with headers.
```

Codex equivalent:

```text
$specify Add CSV export to HarborTasks with all matching rows and authorized fields.
```

## What happens

The skill frames the problem, identifies ambiguities, gathers needed evidence, and writes one specification. It separates product decisions from agent/tool decisions. For the export example, deciding “63 matching tasks, not 20 visible rows” is a product requirement, not a query implementation detail.

## What you get

Illustrative artifact shape:

```text
docs/specs/csv-export.md
  Functional layer: scenarios, acceptance criteria, non-goals
  UX layer: user flow, empty/error states
  UI layer: surface notes or N/A with reason
  Open decisions: named and reviewable
```

## Review before continuing

Check that the core scenario is yours, non-goals are explicit, acceptance criteria are falsifiable, and open questions are not disguised as requirements. Approve product decisions before downstream design.

## Tips and recovery

If the output describes implementation too early, ask it to move that material to assumptions or next steps. If the UX layer is missing without a reason, the spec is incomplete.

## Where to go next

Use [define-architecture](#skill-define-architecture) for system shape, [design-slice](#skill-design-slice) for feature contracts, or [ui-design](#skill-ui-design) for user-facing surfaces.
